back: The list of characters a system can represent, with a binary code for each.

front: How many characters in ASCII and extended ASCII?
back: ASCII: 7 bits, 128 characters. Extended ASCII: 8 bits, 256 characters.
A character set that gives every character of all languages a unique code point, stored using encodings such as UTF-8 and UTF-16.
UTF-8 uses 1 to 4 bytes per character (ASCII characters use 1); UTF-16 uses 2 or 4 bytes.
To represent the characters of many languages and symbols, and to avoid clashes between different 8-bit character sets.

front: How are upper-case and lower-case letters related in ASCII?
back: The code of a lower-case letter is 32 more than the code of the same upper-case letter, so one bit differs.
An 8-bit IBM character code used on older mainframes; it is not compatible with ASCII.

front: How do you calculate the storage for a text?
back: Multiply the number of characters by the bits (or bytes) per character, then convert to the unit asked for.

front: Do you need to memorise ASCII codes?
back: No: a code table is given. You need to know the order (digits, capitals, lower case) and that case differs by 32.
